newsitem.title: TAIWAN: New Taiwan watchdog to tackle stock speculation.
newsitem.headline: New Taiwan watchdog to tackle stock speculation.

text.p: Taiwan's new securities watchdog said on Thursday his agency would crack down on illegal stock investment clubs to curb what he said was blatant and harmful price manipulation.

Lu Tung-ying, taking up the reins of the Securities and Exchange Commission, said underground groups had hampered stock market development and soured foreign interest in the island's bourse, the state-funded Central News Agency reported.

Illegal stock investment clubs have exploited Taiwan's mushrooming and poorly regulated cable television stations to manipulate share prices by prodding members during trading hours to buy or sell certain stocks, Lu said.
Such programmes "have hurt every investor in the market," Lu said.
"If the problem remains unresolved, it will affect the confidence of both domestic and foreign investors," he said.
Brokers said many speculative shares already had fallen since Lu's appointment was announced on Saturday.

"The market likes to call him Captain Lu," said Michael Hung of Nikko Securities. "He will be very tough on stock speculation but I don't think that will have a significant impact on the overall market."
On Thursday, the weighted index ended up 76.18 points, or 1.22 percent, at 6,304.96.
Lu said the commission would simplify procedures to attract more companies to list on the main stock exchange and on Taiwan's fledgling over-the-counter market.
The agency also would try to increase the presence of institutions in the market, he said.
